question.problem: Given that the continuous random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[\frac{1}{3},\frac{7}{3}],$ compute $P(X>1).$
question.worked_solution:
The probability density function for a uniformly distributed continuous random variable $X$ on an interval $[a,b]$ is given by

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{b-a},\, & a\le x\le b, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

Our random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[\frac{1}{3},\frac{7}{3}],$ so it has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2},\, & \frac{1}{3}\le x\le \frac{7}{3}, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>1) & =P(1<X\le \frac{7}{3}) \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{7/3}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{7/3}\frac{1}{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{(\frac{7}{3}-1)}{2} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
